receipt: tick 600 BUILT (t599 measured it absent; before that the map carried it `unknown` while csp.rs's own header already documented frame-ancestors as unimplemented). Both mechanisms enforced at ONE point — the async subframe pass, where the response headers are still in hand — via `framing_allowed`. THE THING WRITTEN FROM INTUITION GETS WRONG, and it is gated: `frame-ancestors` OVERRIDES X-Frame-Options ENTIRELY (CSP3 7.4.1), including overriding a DENY. Taking the stricter of the two is the obvious implementation and it breaks every site that migrated to the directive and left the legacy header behind, which IS the normal migration path. Supported: DENY, SAMEORIGIN (origin-compared against the EMBEDDER, not the frame), frame-ancestors 'none'/'self'/*/host-sources incl. *.suffix. An unrecognised X-Frame-Options value is IGNORED, not treated as DENY — a typo must not silently un-frame a working embed; an unrecognised frame-ancestors SOURCE does not match, because there the page said 'only these may frame me'. A refused frame renders NOTHING and the element stays empty: rendering the body anyway 'so the user sees something' is exactly the failure the header exists to prevent. RED-proven (bypass the check -> all seven test frames render instead of four). GATE also carries a vacuity guard — a header-less frame must still render, or an implementation that blocked everything would pass every 'was it blocked?' claim while making the browser useless. RESIDUE: no error page in the refused frame (Chrome draws one); ALLOW-FROM unsupported (removed from every engine); no reporting.

what_breaks_without_it: CDN-hosted framework bundles routinely carry `integrity`; mishandling means the app's main script never executes and the page is blank
receipt: tick 599 MEASURED then BUILT. Surface audit #33 flagged this as carried `unknown` — the worst status available for a SECURITY control, since nobody knows whether it works, nobody can rely on it and nobody is alarmed. The measurement found it ABSENT (no `integrity` handling anywhere in the tree), so every SRI-protected script on the web was executing unverified, SILENTLY: a substituted script runs, nothing throws, nothing is logged, and the page that did everything right cannot tell. Now enforced in `fetch_external_scripts` — the choke point where classic `<script src>` bytes land — over the RAW response body, never `decoded_text()` (a UTF-8 transcode changes the bytes, and a security control that fires on BOM-prefixed innocent content teaches everyone to remove it). SRI 3.3.4 strength selection is implemented, not approximated: the STRONGEST algorithm present decides, because 'any listed hash matches' would let a page's own stale sha256 fallback downgrade its sha512 — an attack on the mechanism, not a nicety. Per 3.3.3 an attribute with no RECOGNISED metadata (`integrity=""`, `md5-...`) is no requirement at all and must not block; failing closed there bricks pages while protecting nobody. Both base64 alphabets accepted. RED-proven (bypass the check -> the tampered script runs: `ABCDEF` instead of `ACDEF`). RESIDUE: `<link rel=stylesheet integrity>` and module scripts are not covered — classic `<script src>` is the dominant SRI carrier and the only one routed through this choke point today.
